newsitem.title: KENYA: Strong dollar demand dragging down Kenya shilling.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar demand dragging down Kenya shilling.

text.p: Strong dollar demand in the face of dwindling dollar supply continued to pressure the Kenyan shilling downwards on Friday, commercial bank dealers said.
"It's a bit crazy. This whole week, we've seen demand on a daily basis -- and not from traditional importers -- with no matching demand," one dealer said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.79 from 54.74 against the dollar while against the pound it was posted at 89.32 from 88.80.
Another dealer said the market had seen some panic buying for the dollar which could be blamed on a government announcement this week that it would lift a ban on maize imports.
"Most importers are anticipating that the food bill will be rather high so they are rushing to buy dollars at the current rate, which is pretty cheap," he added.
But dealers said the shilling's gradual depreciation seen over the last two weeks did not warrant any reason for alarm.
"All we'll continue to see is the shillings under pressure but a calm market. We might, however, see a jittery market once the election date is announced," one dealer said.
He was referring to the coming general elections to be held some time this year.
The money market continued to experience a shortage of liquid funds for overnight lending. Overnight rates were quoted at above 25 percent unchanged for the fourth consecutive day.
